affreight: To hire, as a ship, for the transportation of goods or freight.
affirmation: 1. Confirmation of anything established; ratification; as, the affirmation of a law. Hooker. 2. The act of affirming or asserting as true; assertion; -- opposed to negation or denial. 3. afoul: In collision; entangled. Totten. To run afoul of, to run against or come into collision with, especially so as to become entangled or to cause injury.
afforestation: The act of converting into forest or woodland. Blackstone.
affectionateness: The quality of being affectionate; fondness; affection.
affecter: One who affects, assumes, pretends, or strives after. "Affecters of wit." Abp. Secker.
affiliation: 1. Adoption; association or reception as a member in or of the same family or society. 2. (Law) The establishment or ascertaining of parentage; the assignment of a child, as a bastard, to its father; filiation. 3. Connection in the way of descent. H. Spencer.
afflux: A flowing towards; that which flows to; as, an afflux of blood to the head.
afflict: 1. To strike or cast down; to overthrow. (old) "Reassembling our afflicted powers." Milton. 2. afterbirth: The placenta and membranes with which the fetus is connected, and which come away after delivery.
aforesaid: Said before, or in a preceding part; already described or identified.
affirmant: 1. One who affirms or asserts. 2. (Law) One who affirms of taking an oath.
afterdamp: An irrespirable gas, remaining after an explosion of fire damp in mines; choke damp. See Carbonic acid.
afloat: 1. Borne on the water; floating; on board ship. On such a full sea are we now afloat. Shak. 2. Moving; passing from place to place; in general circulation; as, a rumor is afloat. 3. Unfixed; moving without guide or control; adrift; as, our affairs are all afloat.
affectioned: 1. Disposed. (old) Be kindly affectioned one to another. Rom. xii. 10. 2. Affected; conceited. (old) Shak.
affiliate: 1. To adopt; to receive into a family as a son; hence, to bring or receive into close connection; to ally. Is the soul affiliated to God, or is it estranged and in rebellion I. Taylor. 2. | To connect or associate one's self; -- followed by with; as, they affiliate with no party.
affectional: Of or pertaining to the affections; as, affectional impulses; an affectional nature.
affreightment: The act of hiring, or the contract for the use of, a vessel, or some part of it, to convey cargo.
affectationist: One who exhibits affectation. Fitzed. Hall.
aftermost: 1. Hindmost; -- opposed to foremost. 2. (Naut.) Nearest the stern; most aft.
afrit: A powerful evil jinnee, demon, or monstrous giant.
affectible: That may be affected. Lay aside the absolute, and, by union with the creaturely, become affectible. Coleridge.
afternote: One of the small notes occur on the unaccented parts of the measure, taking their time from the preceding note.
afterwit: Wisdom or perception that comes after it can be of use. "After- wit comes too late when the mischief is done." L'Estrange.
afflictedness: The state of being afflicted; affliction. (old) Bp. Hall.
afore: 1. Before. (old) If he have never drunk wine afore. Shak. 2. (Naut.) In the fore part of a vessel. | 1. Before (in all its senses). (old) 2. (Naut.) affiliable: Capable of being affiliated to or on, or connected with in origin.
afghan: Of or pertaining to Afghanistan. | 1. A native of Afghanistan. 2. A kind of worsted blanket or wrap.
afoam: In a foaming state; as, the sea is all afoam. A. F. OF L. A. F. of L. (Abbrev.) American Federation of Labor.
affix: 1. africanize: To place under the domination of Africans or negroes. [Amer.] Bartlett.
affrightment: Affright; the state of being frightened; sudden fear or alarm. (old) Passionate words or blows . . . fill the child's mind with terror and affrightment. Locke.
affair: 1. That which is done or is to be done; matter; concern; as, a difficult affair to manage; business of any kind, commercial, professional, or public; -- often in the plural. affectionately: With affection; lovingly; fondly; tenderly; kindly.
afterwise: Wise after the event; wise or knowing, when it is too late.
affirmatively: In an affirmative manner; on the affirmative side of a question; in the affirmative; -- opposed to negatively.
affy: 1. To confide (one's self to, or in); to trust. (old) 2. To betroth or espouse; to affiance. (old) Shak. 3. To bind in faith. (old) Bp. Montagu. | To trust or confide. (old) Shak.
affrap: To strike, or strike down. (old) Spenser.
afresh: Anew; again; once more; newly. They crucify . . . the Son of God afresh. Heb. vi. 6.
affect: 1. To act upon; to produce an effect or change upon. As might affect the earth with cold heat. Milton. The climate affected their health and spirits. Macaulay. 2. | Affection; inclination; passion; feeling; disposition. (old) Shak.
aftercast: A throw of dice after the game in ended; hence, anything done too late. Gower.
afrite: A powerful evil jinnee, demon, or monstrous giant.
afflatus: 1. A breath or blast of wind. 2. A divine impartation of knowledge; supernatural impulse; inspiration. A poet writing against his genius will be like a prophet without his afflatus. Spence.
afford: 1. To give forth; to supply, yield, or produce as the natural result, fruit, or issue; as, grapes afford wine; olives afford oil; the earth affords fruit; the sea affords an abundant supply of fish. 2. To give, grant, or confer, with a remoter reference to its being the natural result; to provide; to furnish; as, a good life affords consolation in old age.
affriended: Made friends; reconciled. (old) "Deadly foes . . . affriended." Spenser.
affected: 1. Regarded with affection; beloved. (old) His affected Hercules. Chapman. 2. Inclined; disposed; attached. How stand you affected his wish Shak. 3. affricate: A combination of a stop, or explosive, with an immediately following fricative or spirant of corresponding organic position, as pf in german Pfeffer, pepper, z (= ts) in German Zeit, time.
aftergrass: The grass that grows after the first crop has been mown; aftermath.
afeard: Afraid. (old) Be not afeard; the isle is full of noises. Shak.
affordment: Anything given as a help; bestowal. (old)
affectibility: The quality or state of being affectible.
africanism: A word, phrase, idiom, or custom peculiar to Africa or Africans. "The knotty Africanisms . . . of the fathers." Milton.
affectingly: In an affecting manner; is a manner to excite emotions.

affinitative: Of the nature of affinity. -- Af*fin"i*ta*tive*ly, adv.

affluxion: The act of flowing towards; afflux. Sir T. Browne.

affrontiveness: The quality that gives an affront or offense. Bailey.

affronte: Face to face, or front to front; facing.
aftercrop: A second crop or harvest in the same year. Mortimer.
aftersails: The sails on the mizzenmast, or on the stays between the mainmast and mizzenmast. Totten.
affirmance: 1. Confirmation; ratification; confirmation of a voidable act. This statute . . . in affirmance of the common law. Bacon. 2. A strong declaration; affirmation. Cowper.
afterglow: A glow of refulgence in the western sky after sunset.
africander: One born in Africa, the offspring of a white father and a "colored" mother. Also, and now commonly in Southern Africa, a native born of European settlers.
african: Of or pertaining to Africa. African hemp, a fiber prerared from the leaves of the Sanseviera Guineensis, a plant found in Africa and India. -- African marigold, a tropical American plant (Tagetes… | A native of Africa; also one ethnologically belonging to an African race.
affirmable: Capable of being affirmed, asserted, or declared; -- followed by of; as, an attribute affirmable of every just man.
affuse: To pour out or upon. I first affused water upon the compressed beans. Boyle.
afferent: Bearing or conducting inwards to a part or organ; -- opposed to efferent; as, afferent vessels; afferent nerves, which convey sensations from the external organs to the brain.
affreighter: One who hires or charters a ship to convey goods.
affirmative: 1. Confirmative; ratifying; as, an act affirmative of common law. 2. affiche: A written or printed notice to be posted, as on a wall; a poster; a placard.
aflame: Inflames; glowing with light or passion; ablaze. G. Eliot.

affectedly: 1. In an affected manner; hypocritically; with more show than reality. 2. Lovingly; with tender care. (old) Shak.

affective: 1. Tending to affect; affecting. (old) Burnet. 2. Pertaining to or exciting emotion; affectional; emotional. Rogers.
affrightful: Terrifying; frightful. -- Af*fright"ful*ly, adv. (old) Bugbears or affrightful apparitions. Cudworth.
aftermentioned: Mentioned afterwards; as, persons after-mentioned (in a writing).
affecting: 1. Moving the emotions; fitted to excite the emotions; pathetic; touching; as, an affecting address; an affecting sight. The most affecting music is generally the most simple. 2. Affected; given to false show. (old) A drawling; affecting rouge. Shak.
affinal: Related by marriage; from the same source.
afar: At, to, or from a great distance; far away; -- often used with from preceding, or off following; as, he was seen from afar; I saw him afar off. The steep where Fame's proud temple shines afar. Beattie.

afflation: A blowing or breathing on; inspiration.

affectation: 1. An attempt to assume or exhibit what is not natural or real; false display; artificial show. "An affectation of contempt." Macaulay. affrontee: One who receives an affront. Lytton.

afterwards: At a later or succeeding time.

affrighten: To frighten. (old) "Fit tales . . . to affrighten babes." Southey.

affectionated: Disposed; inclined. (old) Affectionated to the people. Holinshed.
